lens: Intelligence analyst / structured analytic techniques (Analysis of Competing Hypotheses, Heuer). Core test applied: does an observation change the relative likelihood of competing hypotheses, or is it merely consistent with the favored one? Under ACH, evidence consistent with every hypothesis has zero analytic value regardless of how solid the evidence itself is. I scored the rubric's own formula (CONFIDENCE = .28·DOC + .22·GEO + .18·INF + .14·OWN + .08·TEST + .10·COR, times (1 − CONTAM/200)) against real facilities and real circulating claims and checked whether the output grade matches the defensible answer. It frequently does not. The rubric is a well-built instrument for measuring EVIDENCE VOLUME. It has no term anywhere for EVIDENCE DIAGNOSTICITY, no named alternative hypothesis, and no proposition — it grades a place rather than a claim about a place. Consequence: it is crisp exactly where no adjudication is needed (Raven Rock, obvious fabrications) and collapses into an undifferentiated C–E band exactly where adjudication is the whole product.
verdict: Needs restructuring, not patching. Three of the failures are fatal and they compound: (1) 54% of the weight sits on the three least diagnostic axes (GEO .22 + INF .18 + OWN .14), which measure "there is underground infrastructure at this location" — a proposition that is TRUE of limestone mines, highway tunnels, sewer works, data centers, and large airports, and therefore discriminates nothing; (2) there is no named hypothesis and no proposition, so "CONFIDENCE 62" is confidence in an unstated claim, and the rubric cannot express the single most common real state of affairs in this domain — "the hole is certain, the function is not"; (3) the CONTAM multiplier bottoms out at ×0.5, so a claim traced with perfect rigor to one admitted fabrication retains half its score, and because GEO/INF/OWN score the TERRAIN rather than the CLAIM, any fabrication attached to a real place inherits a floor it cannot fall below. The demonstration is that the AT&T Long Lines hardened underground station at Fairview, Kansas (a genuine, visitable Cold War hardened facility) scores C=56.3, and SubTropolis in Kansas City (a commercial limestone-mine warehouse, not a bunker in any sense) scores C=60.2 — the mundane warehouse outranks the real bunker. Two cases, opposite ground truths, indistinguishable output. That is the definition of a non-diagnostic instrument. The framework worth keeping — three visibly separated evidence buckets, backward-sourcing of folklore, retained F-grades, versioned regrades, the LINEAGE/REFUTER adversarial pair — is genuinely good and rare. It is the scoring math and the axis definitions that need rebuilding, not the philosophy. Do not ratify v0.1. Ratify v0.2 with per-proposition grading, diagnosticity weighting, and an alternative-hypothesis term.

failures.problem: The rubric scores evidence CONSISTENT with the bunker hypothesis and never asks what else the evidence is consistent with. GEO and INF as written (ventilation morphology, portal shape, anomalous road grade into terrain, spoil, dedicated substation, deep wells, rail spur, generators, fuel permits) describe features shared by every large underground works project. Together with OWN they carry 54% of the weight. There is no P(evidence | not-H) term anywhere in the system.
failures.worked_example:
Two real sites, opposite ground truths, scored under the rubric as written.

CASE A — AT&T Long Lines hardened underground station, Fairview, Kansas. A genuine Cold War buried hardened structure: blast doors, own generators, deep well, dedicated power feed, microwave tower, part of the AT&T Long Lines hardened L-carrier network. Documentation is FCC antenna registry (P2), corporate/enthusiast Long Lines documentation (P4), county deeds from its sale (P2). Almost no declassified federal record. Scores: DOC 25, GEO 80, INF 95, OWN 75, TEST 60, COR 55, CONTAM 20 → raw 62.50 → CONFIDENCE 56.25 → GRADE C, "reasonable inference, no primary confirmation." It is not an inference. You can stand in it.

CASE B — SubTropolis, Kansas City, Missouri. A ~55-million-sq-ft former room-and-pillar limestone mine, now commercial warehousing. Truck portals cut into a hillside, ventilation shafts, rail spur, dedicated power, controlled access, has historically hosted federal records tenants. Scores: DOC 20, GEO 85, INF 90, OWN 85, TEST 50, COR 70, CONTAM 10 → raw 63.40 → CONFIDENCE 60.23 → GRADE C.

The commercial warehouse outscores the real hardened bunker by 4 points. Every GEO and INF observation the rubric rewards is satisfied by "large hole in limestone with trucks in it." The axes measure undergroundness, not hardenedness, not federalness, not continuity-of-government function. Under ACH these observations have diagnosticity near zero and should carry near-zero weight; the rubric gives them 40% of the total.
failures.proposed_fix: Attach a diagnosticity coefficient to every individual observation, not to the axis. Observation contribution = strength × diagnosticity, where diagnosticity ∈ [0,1] is assigned against a MANDATORY enumerated alternative-hypothesis set that REFUTER instantiates per candidate: {commercial/industrial mine or quarry, highway or rail tunnel, water/sewer works, subway or utility vault, agricultural or cold storage, data center, already-registered decommissioned silo, civil mine reclamation, nothing at all}. Calibration anchors: ventilation shaft = 0.05; spoil pile = 0.05; anomalous road grade = 0.10; deep well = 0.10; rail spur = 0.10; dedicated substation = 0.15; restricted airspace overlay = 0.35; blast-door or blast-valve line item in a filed permit or GSA disposal record = 0.90; EMP-hardening specification in a procurement document = 0.95; AT&T Long Lines hardened-site lineage = 0.75. A site whose entire GEO/INF case is built from ≤0.15 observations must be structurally incapable of exceeding grade D no matter how many such observations accumulate — currently 200 non-diagnostic observations sum to a B.

failures.problem: CONFIDENCE has no required documentary floor. A candidate can reach grade B — "strongly evidenced" — with DOC exactly 0. Simultaneously, a candidate with DOC 100 and nothing else lands at 28 = grade E, "folklore with a trace." The weighting inverts the relationship between the most diagnostic evidence category and the grade.
failures.worked_example:
Arithmetic first: DOC=0 with all five remaining axes at 100 and CONTAM 0 yields exactly 72.00 → GRADE B, "Strongly evidenced. Existence solid." Zero documents. Conversely DOC=100 alone yields 28.00 → GRADE E.

Real case for the second half — the DEEP UNDERGROUND COMMAND CENTER (DUCC). Proposed 31 January 1962, a 50-to-300-man national command bunker 3,000–4,000 ft beneath the Washington area, sited under the Potomac between the Pentagon and the White House, specified to survive multiple direct hits by 200–300 MT surface bursts. Recommended to President Kennedy for FY1965 funding shortly before his assassination; Congress declined to appropriate; never built. The declassified paper trail is exceptional and impeccably P1: JCS and OSD memoranda, DoD budget submissions, the FY1965 appropriations record showing the rejection, LBJ Library holdings, associated SAC DUSC and NORAD SCC proposals.

Scored as written: DOC 95, GEO 0 (nothing was ever dug), INF 0, OWN 5, TEST 30, COR 60, CONTAM 0 → 35.70 → GRADE E, "folklore with a trace. Claim has an identifiable origin and nothing more."

DUCC is not folklore. It is among the best-documented continuity-of-government programs in the entire declassified US record. The rubric assigns it the same band it assigns Dulce Base. It has also silently conflated two different questions — "how good is the evidence" and "does the thing physically exist" — and there is nowhere to record the answer, because the Status enum (active · decommissioned · converted · sealed · demolished · unknown · alleged-only) has no value for PROPOSED / CANCELLED / NEVER BUILT. A register of hardened facilities that cannot represent the bunkers that were designed, costed, debated and killed is missing a large and fully documented slice of its own subject.
failures.proposed_fix: Two changes. (a) Split the single score into per-proposition grades and grade each independently: EXISTS-AS-PHYSICAL-STRUCTURE / IS-HARDENED / IS-FEDERAL-OR-STATE / FUNCTION-AS-CLAIMED / OPERATIONAL-STATUS. DUCC then reads EXISTS=F, DOCUMENTED-AS-PROGRAM=A, which is the true and useful answer. Grade B's own prose ("existence solid, function partly inferred") already presupposes this split — the math just cannot produce it. (b) Add PROPOSED-NEVER-BUILT and PROPOSED-STATUS-UNKNOWN to the Status enum, plus a CANCELLED era-independent flag, and let a program-level entity exist without coordinates.

failures.problem: The CONTAM multiplier floors at ×0.5, so contamination can never move a candidate more than one-and-a-bit grade bands. Combined with GEO/INF/OWN scoring the LOCATION rather than the CLAIM, any fabrication anchored to a real geographic place inherits a score floor it cannot fall through. F becomes unreachable for the entire class of claims the register most needs to grade F.
failures.worked_example:
DULCE BASE, Archuleta Mesa, New Mexico. Origin is fully traced and the trace is short: Albuquerque businessman Paul Bennewitz, from 1979, convinced he was intercepting alien transmissions; his claims reach popular press by 1983; John Lear claims "independent confirmation" in 1987; Lear's statement influences Thomas Allen LeVesque writing as "Jason Bishop III," who LATER ADMITTED FABRICATING Dulce material; the "Thomas Castello" security-officer documents surface 1987, and both a retired USAF colonel and New Mexico State Police officer Gabe Valdez stated no such person was ever employed there; images attributed to Castello include a still from the 2000 film The 6th Day.

Now score it as a rule-following ASSESSOR would. The DOC firewall caps P4/P5-only at 40 — but an ARCHIVIST hunting documents ABOUT DULCE finds genuine P1/P2 material: Project Gasbuggy, the 1967 AEC underground nuclear detonation in the Carson National Forest roughly twenty miles from Dulce, with a full AEC/DOE paper trail; Jicarilla Apache Nation and BLM land records; and the real, documented 1970s New Mexico State Police cattle-mutilation investigation files under Gabe Valdez. None of it is evidence for a base. The rubric never asks EVIDENCE FOR WHAT, so DOC 45. Archuleta Mesa is real terrain with real road cuts and real regional mining scarring: GEO 40. Jicarilla gas-field wells, roads, power: INF 35. Title chain is documentable: OWN 30. TEST reads "named worker accounts" — Castello presents as precisely that, alongside Bennewitz, Lear, Cherry Hinkle, Valdez: TEST 55. COR counts lineages and an agent sees four or five apparent ones: COR 50.

With CONTAM 85: 41.30 → 23.75 → GRADE E.
With CONTAM 100 — the LINEAGE agent doing a flawless job, every source collapsed to one origin: 41.30 → 20.65 → STILL GRADE E.

Perfect contamination analysis cannot reach F. The ×0.5 floor makes the conspiracy handler structurally incapable of handling the conspiracy. And Dulce is the easy case: a fabrication attached to a site with genuinely strong GEO/INF — invent a claim about a real active installation and the floor rises further.
failures.proposed_fix: (a) Make CONTAM able to zero the score: multiplier (1 − CONTAM/100), not /200. A claim whose every lineage collapses to one origin has, by construction, one source — and one source is not corroboration at any volume. (b) Gate the axes by what the evidence is evidence OF. Every source must be tagged with the proposition it supports; Project Gasbuggy supports PROPOSITION{underground nuclear test occurred at coordinates X, 1967} and contributes ZERO to PROPOSITION{alien base under Archuleta Mesa}. Proximity is not support. (c) Give the citogenesis flag arithmetic teeth — currently it is 'flagged loudly' and does not appear in the formula at all, so a laundered claim scores identically to a clean one at equal CONTAM. Make it a hard cap: citogenesis confirmed ⇒ maximum grade E on the laundered proposition, irrespective of score.

failures.problem: COR counts sources and calls it independence, and the agent architecture actively manufactures false corroboration. §2 states Tier 1 agents are "blind to the others' findings during discovery — that independence is what makes the COR axis mean anything." That is a category error: agent independence is not source independence. Seven blind crawlers over a corpus seeded by one origin each independently return the same claim, and COR rises for a reason that has nothing to do with the evidence.
failures.worked_example:
DENVER INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT — the "vast underground bunker / DUMB beneath the terminal" claim, in circulation since the mid-1990s from a small identifiable origin set of self-published books and derivative media.

Watch the blind fleet corroborate itself. ARCHIVIST returns genuine GAO audit reports on DIA cost overruns and the failed automated baggage system (P1). CARTOGRAPHER returns real large-footprint underground structures and tunnels (P2). CIRCUIT returns a genuinely enormous dedicated electrical load, a dedicated fuel farm and pipeline, and deep wells (P1/P2 permits). LEDGER returns real construction contracts that were sequenced, terminated and reissued during a chaotic build (P1, FPDS/USAspending). VERNACULAR returns contemporaneous 1990s Denver press describing buried structures (P3). PALIMPSEST returns the conspiracy corpus and correctly traces its origin. Six of seven agents independently return signals. Not one of them discriminates between {hardened federal facility} and {largest-footprint airport in North America, built badly} — the second hypothesis explains all six observations completely and more economically.

Scored: DOC 60, GEO 70, INF 80, OWN 65, TEST 40, COR 65. With CONTAM 60 → 45.78 → GRADE D. But CONTAM 30 is the MORE defensible reading, because the P1/P2 infrastructure lineages genuinely ARE independent of each other and of the conspiracy corpus — and then: 55.59 → GRADE C, "reasonable inference. Converging open signals."

A published C-grade register entry for a hardened underground facility at Denver International Airport would be, on its own, sufficient to destroy the credibility of the entire project. And it arrives not from a rogue agent but from every rule being followed correctly. The deeper bug: CONTAM is one global number over a heterogeneous evidence base where the mundane parts are genuinely independent and the extraordinary parts are not. Averaging them dilutes contamination away from exactly the claim that needed it.
failures.proposed_fix: (a) Redefine COR as the count of lineages that are independent AND diagnostic — a lineage contributes only if it would not exist under the leading alternative hypothesis. Six independent confirmations that an airport has fuel tanks is COR 0. (b) Compute CONTAM per proposition, never per candidate. DIA then reads: PROPOSITION{large underground works exist} CONTAM 5, grade A; PROPOSITION{hardened non-airport federal facility} CONTAM 95, grade F. Both true, both published, no contradiction. (c) Delete the claim that discovery-agent blindness produces source independence — it is false and it will be quoted back at the project. Blindness reduces anchoring between agents, which is worth having, and does nothing whatsoever for COR.

failures.problem: The P1–P5 firewall gates only DOC. GEO, INF, OWN, TEST and COR have no provenance gating at all — including COR, the axis most vulnerable to laundering, and TEST, which is definitionally almost all P5.
failures.worked_example:
Under the rubric as written a candidate can score GEO 100 entirely from a P4 urbex blog's photo captions and P5 forum coordinate guesses, INF 100 from an enthusiast wiki's assertion of a substation, and COR 100 by counting P5 forum posts as lineages — total 40.0 before CONTAM from purely P4/P5 material, and 72.0 if OWN and TEST are also filled from the same tier, i.e. GRADE B on nothing but forum posts and blogs. The DOC firewall never fires because DOC stayed at 0.

TEST specifically: the axis rewards "named worker accounts." Thomas Castello is a named worker account. Phil Schneider, who claimed to be a geologist/engineer at Dulce and whose employment has never been independently corroborated, is a named worker account. So is a genuine Site R communications NCO whose assignment appears in a unit history and an obituary. The axis as written cannot tell these apart, because it scores the FORM of the testimony rather than its RESOLVABILITY.
failures.proposed_fix: Apply tier caps to every axis, not just DOC: P4/P5-only caps of GEO 30, INF 30, OWN 20, TEST 25, COR 15. Redefine TEST to score resolvability rather than form: full credit only when the named individual is independently locatable in a record that both PREDATES the claim and was created for an unrelated purpose (payroll, unit history, union roll, obituary, court filing, property record). A name that resolves to nothing outside the claim scores TEST 0, not TEST 55.

failures.problem: REFUTER has no arithmetic power and runs at the wrong threshold. §3 W2 multi-votes REFUTER only "for anything above grade C" — but grade C and below is exactly where mundane explanations live and where the register's credibility is actually at risk. And there is no term anywhere in CONFIDENCE for "a mundane explanation fully accounts for every observation," so REFUTER can mark a candidate refuted without the number moving at all.
failures.worked_example: Both the SubTropolis case (60.23, C) and the DIA case (55.59, C) sit AT OR BELOW the C boundary and therefore receive single-vote refutation under W2 — while Raven Rock at 89.60 gets the multi-vote adversarial treatment it has no need of whatsoever. The scrutiny is allocated in inverse proportion to where error is possible. And even when REFUTER wins on SubTropolis — "this is a commercial limestone warehouse, here is the operator, here are the leases, here are the tenants" — the formula still returns 60.23, because nothing in it subtracts for a fully sufficient alternative explanation. The refutation lands in a text field beside a C grade.
failures.proposed_fix: (a) Invert the multi-vote threshold: mandatory multi-vote REFUTER for every candidate in the C–E band, plus grade A. (b) Add a scored ALT axis — the strength of the best surviving mundane explanation, 0–100 — and make it multiplicative: CONFIDENCE × (1 − ALT/100). SubTropolis with ALT 95 drops from 60.23 to 3.0. DIA's hardened-facility proposition with ALT 95 drops to 2.8. (c) Require REFUTER to output the enumerated alternative set with each alternative explicitly scored and dispositioned, and publish it on the entry page — that table is the single most valuable artifact the register could show a skeptical reader.

failures.problem: The weight vector is asserted rather than derived, and is close to inverted relative to diagnosticity. The axes are also not independent, so the weighted sum double-counts.
failures.worked_example:
DOC — the only axis whose contents are routinely high-diagnosticity (a NEPA filing specifying blast valves; a GSA disposal record naming a hardened special facility; an appropriations line item) — carries .28. The three lowest-diagnosticity axes carry .54 combined. TEST at .08 is nearly weightless despite being, in the Greenbrier case, the evidence that actually broke the story.

Independence failure, concrete: for the AT&T Fairview KS site, the microwave-relay lineage scores INF, the tower scores GEO (portal/structure morphology at the surface), the FCC antenna registration scores DOC, and the AT&T-to-private title transfer scores OWN. Four axes, one underlying fact — the site was an AT&T Long Lines station — counted four times across .28+.22+.18+.14 = .82 of the total weight. The rubric's claim that the six axes are "independent" is not true of the evidence types it lists under them.

And the Greenbrier / Project Greek Island shows the weights cannot track a real regime change: pre-1992 (Ted Gup's Washington Post disclosure) the evidence was GEO/INF/TEST-shaped — a large structure under the West Virginia Wing, anomalous power and comms, local workers who talked — scoring 38.85 → E, "folklore with a trace." That was wrong; the correct pre-1992 state was existence B, function F. Post-disclosure it scores 88.82 → A. A 50-point discontinuity from one newspaper article means the pre-disclosure score was measuring publicity, not evidence.
failures.proposed_fix: Derive the weights by back-fitting to a ratified calibration set (below) rather than asserting them, and re-derive after every 25 adjudications. Route each source to exactly ONE axis with an explicit deduplication rule so a single underlying fact cannot enter the sum four times. Consider raising DOC toward .40 and collapsing GEO+INF into a single SIGNATURE axis at ~.20 once diagnosticity weighting is in place, since with diagnosticity applied the two are measuring the same thing.

failures.problem: No base rate, no prior, and no discovery-side confirmation-bias control. Tier 1 agents are tasked to FIND candidates; nothing rewards an agent for returning "I looked and there is nothing here." The COMPLETENESS CRITIC's brief ("what region is underrepresented") explicitly pushes toward filling map gaps, which under a find-rewarded fleet manufactures candidates in sparse regions.
failures.worked_example:
There are on the order of a few hundred genuinely hardened federal facilities in CONUS against many tens of thousands of underground structures — mines, quarries, highway and rail tunnels, utility vaults, cold-storage caverns, decommissioned civil-defense basements. The prior odds that an arbitrary anomalous underground signature is a hardened federal facility are on the order of 1:100 or worse. The rubric never encodes this, so a candidate assembled from purely non-diagnostic signals starts at an implied 50/50 rather than at 1:100. The SubTropolis and DIA results above are that missing prior made visible: both begin from a prior that should have put them at F and neither is ever charged for it.

Mechanically, the same effect will show up as regional inflation — instruct the COMPLETENESS CRITIC that Montana is underrepresented, task a find-rewarded fleet at Montana, and it will return Montana candidates, because abandoned mine adits with road grades and spoil are abundant there and the rubric scores exactly that.
failures.proposed_fix: (a) Encode an explicit prior per typology and per region, published on the methodology page, and score in log-likelihood-ratio (decibans) rather than 0–100 points so that evidence UPDATES the prior instead of replacing it. Non-diagnostic evidence then contributes ~0 dB by construction, which is the correct answer and requires no special-casing. (b) Add a NULL RETURN requirement: every Tier 1 agent reports sites it examined and rejected, with reasons. Null returns are the base-rate denominator and the only real confirmation-bias control available. (c) Track per-agent grade distributions over time as a bias telemetry signal — an agent whose candidates grade systematically higher than the fleet is over-claiming, and that is measurable.

failures.problem: Grade-band boundaries produce a compressed dynamic range: the practical ceiling for a real-but-obscure facility and the practical floor for a fabrication attached to a real place both land in the C–E band, which is where nearly the entire register will sit and where the rubric has no discriminating power.
failures.worked_example:
From the computed cases: real AT&T hardened bunker 56.25 (C). Mundane limestone warehouse 60.23 (C). DIA conspiracy claim 45.78–55.59 (D/C). Dulce Base 20.65–23.75 (E). DUCC, impeccably documented, 35.70 (E). Greenbrier pre-disclosure 38.85 (E). Six cases spanning ground truths from "unambiguously real" to "admitted fabrication" compress into a 21–60 point window, and within that window rank order is essentially uncorrelated with truth — the warehouse beats the bunker, and DUCC ties the alien base.

Meanwhile the two cases the rubric gets RIGHT are the two that need no rubric: Raven Rock at 89.60 → A (correct — congressional budget lines, GAO reports, EIS filings, unit histories, public acknowledgment), and the "129 Deep Underground Military Bases linked by a national tunnel network" claim at 1.84 → F (correct — no coordinates, no records, originator credentials unverified, traces to a small 1990s origin set). Both are unmistakable to any reader in ten seconds. The rubric's value has to be created in the middle band, and the middle band is where it is noise.
failures.proposed_fix: After introducing diagnosticity weighting, the ALT term, and per-proposition scoring, re-derive the band boundaries empirically against the calibration set so that the boundaries fall where real cases actually separate. Publish per-axis subscores and the alternative-hypothesis table on every entry page rather than leading with the composite letter — the composite is the least informative thing the system computes, and the archival-finding-aid aesthetic the project is targeting favors the decomposition anyway.

failures.problem: Minor but load-bearing: several taxonomy and bookkeeping gaps that the worked examples surfaced and that will be expensive to retrofit after ingest starts.
failures.worked_example: (1) Status enum has no PROPOSED / CANCELLED / NEVER-BUILT — DUCC, SAC's Deep Underground Support Center, and NORAD's Survivable Command Centers are all fully documented and all homeless in the schema. (2) Location precision has no NON-LOCATED value distinct from "claimed-only" — a facility documented in a declassified record whose coordinates are genuinely unknown is not the same epistemic object as one whose coordinates are asserted by a forum post, but the enum forces them together. (3) There is no ENTITY LEVEL distinction between a PROGRAM (Project Greek Island), a SITE (The Greenbrier), and a STRUCTURE (the West Virginia Wing bunker) — a register that cannot separate these will produce merge disasters in RESOLVER and will make the Montauk-style split entries (Camp Hero AFS, real, grade A; "Montauk Project," grade F, same coordinates) impossible to represent. (4) CONTAM is undefined for a candidate with a single source: is one source CONTAM 100 (all evidence from one origin, literally true) or is CONTAM undefined? The definition implies 100, which means every newly discovered single-document candidate is born maximally contaminated.
failures.proposed_fix: Add PROPOSED, CANCELLED and NEVER-BUILT to Status; add NON-LOCATED to Location precision; add an entity_level enum {program, site, structure} with parent-child relations before schema freeze; and define CONTAM as undefined/null below three sources rather than 100, with the single-source case handled by the axis caps instead.

recommendations: Do not ratify v0.1. The philosophy is sound and unusually good; the arithmetic is not, and the arithmetic is what will be run ten thousand times unsupervised.

Replace the 0-100 additive score with log-likelihood-ratio scoring in decibans against an explicit published prior. Non-diagnostic evidence then contributes ~0 by construction rather than by exception, which removes the single largest class of error without any special-casing.

Attach a diagnosticity coefficient to every OBSERVATION (not every axis), assigned against a mandatory enumerated alternative-hypothesis set. Publish the calibration anchors: ventilation shaft 0.05, spoil 0.05, road grade 0.10, deep well 0.10, rail spur 0.10, dedicated substation 0.15, restricted airspace 0.35, blast-door line item in a filed permit 0.90, EMP-hardening spec in a procurement doc 0.95.

Split the single grade into per-proposition grades: EXISTS / IS-HARDENED / IS-FEDERAL / FUNCTION-AS-CLAIMED / STATUS. This is the highest-value single change. It makes DUCC (documented program, never built), Greenbrier pre-1992 (structure yes, function no), and Camp Hero/Montauk (site yes, claims no) all representable, and it eliminates the entire class of 'confidence in an unstated proposition' errors.

Change the CONTAM multiplier from (1 - CONTAM/200) to (1 - CONTAM/100) so a perfectly traced single-origin fabrication can actually reach F, and compute CONTAM per proposition rather than per candidate so that mundane independent evidence cannot dilute the contamination of the extraordinary claim.
Add a scored ALT axis - strength of the best surviving mundane explanation - applied multiplicatively as (1 - ALT/100). This is what gives REFUTER arithmetic power instead of a text field.

Invert the REFUTER multi-vote threshold: mandatory adversarial multi-vote for the C-E band where mundane explanations live, not only above C. Publish REFUTER's alternative-hypothesis table on every entry page; it is the most credibility-generating artifact the register can display.
Extend the P4/P5 firewall to every axis, not just DOC. Suggested caps on P4/P5-only evidence: GEO 30, INF 30, OWN 20, TEST 25, COR 15.

Redefine TEST to score RESOLVABILITY, not form. Full credit only when the named individual appears in an independent record that predates the claim and was created for an unrelated purpose. 'Thomas Castello' and a Site R NCO in a unit history must not score alike.

Redefine COR to count lineages that are independent AND diagnostic - a lineage counts only if it would not exist under the leading alternative hypothesis. Delete the assertion in section 2 that discovery-agent blindness creates source independence; it is false and it will be quoted back at the project.

Give the citogenesis flag arithmetic teeth: confirmed citogenesis hard-caps the laundered proposition at grade E regardless of score. At present it is 'flagged loudly' and does not enter the formula at all.

Require NULL RETURNS from every Tier 1 agent - sites examined and rejected, with reasons. These are the base-rate denominator and the only genuine confirmation-bias control in a fleet that is otherwise rewarded exclusively for finding things. Track per-agent grade distributions as bias telemetry.

Deduplicate evidence across axes with an explicit routing rule. One underlying fact (the AT&T Fairview site was a Long Lines station) currently enters DOC, GEO, INF and OWN simultaneously, across 82% of the total weight.
Freeze the calibration set below as a regression suite BEFORE schema freeze, and re-derive the weight vector by back-fitting to it rather than asserting it. Re-derive after every 25 adjudications.

Fix the schema gaps now, not later: PROPOSED/CANCELLED/NEVER-BUILT in Status; NON-LOCATED in Location precision; an entity_level enum {program, site, structure} with parent-child relations so split entries at shared coordinates are representable.

Lead every entry page with the per-axis decomposition, the alternative-hypothesis table, and the lineage graph - not the composite letter. The composite is the least informative number the system produces, and the archival finding-aid aesthetic the project is targeting is better served by the decomposition anyway.

calibration_set.name: Raven Rock Mountain Complex (Site R), Adams County, Pennsylvania
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL - HIGH. The rubric already gets this right (89.60 as scored) and it should stay right after any revision. Congressional appropriations line items, GAO and IG reports, NEPA/EIS filings, unit histories, named personnel accounts, public DoD acknowledgment, resolved coordinates, unambiguous COG/military-hardened typology, active status. Every proposition scores A: EXISTS A, IS-HARDENED A, IS-FEDERAL A, FUNCTION A, STATUS A. If a revised rubric moves this below A, the revision is broken.

calibration_set.name: "129 Deep Underground Military Bases linked by a national maglev tunnel network" (Sauder / Schneider corpus)
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL - LOW. The rubric already gets this right (1.84 as scored). No coordinates for any of the 129, no procurement record for a construction program of the asserted scale, no spoil-volume accounting, originator employment credentials never independently corroborated, traces to a small self-published 1990s origin set. Retained with origin documented per the F-grade policy. If a revised rubric moves this above F, the revision is broken.

calibration_set.name: Cheyenne Mountain Complex, El Paso County, Colorado
calibration_set.reasoning: POSITIVE CONTROL - HIGH. Publicly acknowledged, extensively documented in congressional and DoD records, publicly toured for decades, engineering literature on the spring-mounted buildings and blast doors. Tests that the rubric does not penalize a facility for being famous.

calibration_set.name: Mount Weather Emergency Operations Center (High Point Special Facility), Bluemont, Virginia
calibration_set.reasoning: Acknowledged FEMA facility. Documentation includes congressional testimony, EIS filings, federal real property records, and the incidental press exposure following the 1974 TWA 514 crash on the mountain. EXISTS A, IS-FEDERAL A, FUNCTION A. Interior extent and current mission detail remain partly inferred - a revised rubric should be able to express that as FUNCTION-DETAIL B while the top-line stays A.

calibration_set.name: The Greenbrier / Project Greek Island, White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia
calibration_set.reasoning: Disclosed May 1992 by Ted Gup in the Washington Post; subsequently decommissioned, declassified, and operated as a public tour. Primary documentation, named participants, physical access. STATUS decommissioned. Also serves as a REGIME-CHANGE TEST: the register should be able to reconstruct the pre-1992 state as EXISTS B / FUNCTION F and show a versioned jump on the 1992 disclosure. Under v0.1 the pre-1992 state scores 38.85 = E, which is wrong; the correct pre-disclosure answer is that the structure was strongly evidenced and the function was unsupported.

calibration_set.name: Titan II Missile Site 571-7, Green Valley, Arizona (Titan Missile Museum)
calibration_set.reasoning: Fully documented Air Force real property, complete construction and deactivation record, publicly toured, coordinates exact. STATUS decommissioned/converted, typology missile silo. Tests that the rubric handles the converted-silo class cleanly - a large fraction of the register will be Atlas/Titan/Minuteman sites and they must not clog the middle bands.

calibration_set.name: National Underground / Iron Mountain, Boyers, Pennsylvania (OPM retirement records operations in a former limestone mine)
calibration_set.reasoning: Real underground federal operations in a converted limestone mine. Documented via GAO reports, congressional testimony on retirement claim processing, contract records, and press with named officials. Typology storage & archive, not COG. IMPORTANT PAIRED TEST with SubTropolis: both are limestone mines with federal-adjacent tenants, but Boyers has direct P1 documentation of the federal operation and SubTropolis does not. A rubric that cannot separate these two on documentary grounds - and instead separates them on GEO/INF, where they are identical - is measuring the wrong thing.

calibration_set.name: Kirtland Underground Munitions and Maintenance Storage Complex (KUMMSC), Kirtland AFB, New Mexico
calibration_set.reasoning: Acknowledged, appears in DoD/DOE documentation and environmental filings, existence and general function certain, but internal extent, capacity and current inventory are inferred rather than documented. This is the intended meaning of grade B - existence solid, extent partly inferred - and it is the band v0.1 can reach only by accident.

calibration_set.name: AT&T Long Lines hardened underground L-carrier station, Fairview, Kansas
calibration_set.reasoning: CRITICAL NEGATIVE-CONTROL PAIR (with SubTropolis). A genuine Cold War buried hardened structure - blast doors, own generators, deep well, dedicated power, part of the AT&T Long Lines hardened network. Existence is certain and physically verifiable; the documentation is corporate, FCC registry and county deed rather than declassified federal, so B rather than A is defensible on evidence quality. What is NOT defensible is v0.1's 56.25 = C, 'reasonable inference, no primary confirmation.' A correct rubric must place this ABOVE SubTropolis by a wide margin. v0.1 places it BELOW.

calibration_set.name: SubTropolis, Kansas City, Missouri — evaluated as a hardened/COG candidate
calibration_set.reasoning: CRITICAL NEGATIVE CONTROL. A ~55-million-sq-ft former room-and-pillar limestone mine operating as commercial warehousing. It scores near-maximum on GEO (portals into hillside, ventilation shafts, spoil history) and INF (rail spur, dedicated power, deep infrastructure) and OWN (clean documented title and lease chain) - and it is not a bunker in any sense. The mundane explanation is complete, documented, and publicly advertised by the operator. Expected F as a hardened/COG candidate, with a note that it is an A-documented commercial underground facility. v0.1 gives it 60.23 = C, outranking the real AT&T bunker. This single pair is the regression test that most sharply discriminates a diagnosticity-aware rubric from a volume-counting one.

calibration_set.name: Deep Underground Command Center (DUCC), proposed 1962 beneath the Washington DC area
calibration_set.expected_grade: A on DOCUMENTED-AS-PROGRAM, F on EXISTS
calibration_set.reasoning: Proposed 31 Jan 1962; 50-to-300-man command bunker at 3,000-4,000 ft, sited under the Potomac between Pentagon and White House, specified against multiple 200-300 MT direct hits; recommended to Kennedy for FY1965; Congress declined to appropriate; never built. Documentation is exceptional P1 - JCS/OSD memoranda, budget submissions, the appropriations record of the rejection, LBJ Library holdings. This is a two-proposition entry and v0.1 cannot represent it: it returns 35.70 = E, the same band as Dulce Base, and the Status enum has no value for NEVER-BUILT. Any revised rubric MUST return A on the program proposition and F on the physical-existence proposition. Include the sibling cancelled programs (SAC's Deep Underground Support Center, NORAD's Survivable Command Centers) as additional instances of the same test.

calibration_set.name: Denver International Airport — "hardened underground federal facility beneath the terminal"
calibration_set.reasoning: CRITICAL NEGATIVE CONTROL. The site genuinely contains large underground works: baggage tunnels, utility tunnels, a dedicated fuel farm and pipeline, deep wells, an enormous electrical load, and a documented history of terminated and reissued construction contracts. Every one of those is fully explained by 'largest-footprint airport in North America, built badly,' which is also the better-documented hypothesis. The extraordinary claim traces to a small identifiable mid-1990s origin set. Expected E, not F, because the origin is documented and genuine large underground works do exist on site - but it must NOT reach D or C. v0.1 returns 45.78 at CONTAM 60 and 55.59 = GRADE C at the more defensible CONTAM 30. A published C-grade DIA bunker entry would on its own destroy the register's credibility, so this case is the single most important thing to test before ratification.

calibration_set.name: Dulce Base, Archuleta Mesa, New Mexico
calibration_set.reasoning: Origin fully traced and short: Paul Bennewitz from 1979, reaching popular press by 1983; John Lear's 1987 claim of 'independent confirmation'; Thomas Allen LeVesque writing as 'Jason Bishop III,' who later ADMITTED FABRICATING Dulce material; the 1987 'Thomas Castello' documents, whose subject both a retired USAF colonel and NM State Police officer Gabe Valdez stated never existed there, and whose attributed images include a still from the 2000 film The 6th Day. CONTAM 100, citogenesis confirmed, admitted fabrication in the lineage. Real P1 material exists in the VICINITY - Project Gasbuggy (1967 AEC underground detonation ~20 mi away), Jicarilla/BLM land records, the genuine NM State Police cattle-mutilation files - and none of it is evidence for the claim. Expected F. v0.1 returns E even at CONTAM 100, because the ×0.5 floor makes F unreachable. Retained with origin documented per policy - this is exactly the entry that justifies the whole backward-sourcing philosophy, and the rubric currently cannot grade it correctly.

calibration_set.name: Camp Hero Air Force Station, Montauk, New York vs. the "Montauk Project"
calibration_set.expected_grade: A on the installation, F on the claims
calibration_set.reasoning: SPLIT-ENTITY TEST at shared coordinates. Camp Hero AFS is a real, fully documented former Air Force installation with a SAGE radar (the AN/FPS-35 tower still standing) and genuine underground structures - grade A, decommissioned, now a state park. The 'Montauk Project' claims of time travel and mind-control research are unsupported and trace to a small 1980s-90s origin set - grade F. The register must publish BOTH at the same location without contradiction. v0.1 has no entity_level and no per-proposition scoring, so it must either merge them into one misleading middle grade or arbitrarily pick one.

calibration_set.name: "Telos, the Lemurian city beneath Mount Shasta, California"
calibration_set.reasoning: Pure literary origin, traceable to Frederick Spencer Oliver's 1894 novel A Dweller on Two Planets and subsequent Lemurian Fellowship literature. CONTAM 100 with a single named 19th-century fictional origin. Tests the cleanest case of the backward-sourcing method: a claim whose origin document is openly a work of fiction. Also tests that a claim attached to real, dramatic, geologically anomalous terrain (a stratovolcano with genuine lava tubes and caves) does not inherit a GEO-driven floor - which under v0.1 it would.

calibration_set.name: Unnamed "Federal Relocation Arc" sites referenced in declassified 1960s Office of Emergency Planning records
calibration_set.reasoning: REAL-BUT-UNLOCATED TEST. Declassified P1 records establish that a set of relocation facilities existed and describe their program function, without individually identifying or locating each one. Correct answer: EXISTS A (documented at program level), LOCATION non-located, individual site identification C at best. Requires the NON-LOCATED location-precision value and the program/site entity split that v0.1 lacks. Under v0.1 these collapse to a low E because GEO, INF and OWN are all necessarily zero for an unlocated site - the same failure mode as DUCC.

calibration_set.name: An unrestored Nike Hercules launch magazine on private agricultural land (e.g. a former Chicago or Kansas City defense-area site)
calibration_set.reasoning: REAL-BUT-THIN TEST. Categorical existence is certain - the Army built hundreds of these and the site lists, real property disposal records and county deeds are public - but site-specific documentation for any individual unrestored magazine is thin, and current condition and status are genuinely unknown. Correct answer: EXISTS A, TYPOLOGY A, STATUS unknown, overall B. Tests that the rubric does not punish a facility for being ordinary and well-attested at the class level rather than dramatically documented at the instance level. Contrast with the restored public site SF-88L, Marin County, California, which should score A - same facility type, different evidence depth, and the rubric should separate them by roughly one band, not four.
